note: Example lexicon for a fictional company. Every rule cites the decision it enforces. If a rule is wrong, fix the decision record first, then this file. Never the reverse.

rules.message: The product was renamed. The old name still ranks in search, and buyers comparing quotes think they are two products.
Retired list price. It still survives on old pages; a customer who quotes it expects it honored.
rules.fix: Link to the pricing page. Do not restate a figure in prose.

rules.pattern: discount floor|walk[\s-]?away price|do not share externally
rules.message: Negotiation logic on a customer-facing page.
rules.fix: Move it under internal/. Not quotable on purpose: a leak inside quotation marks is still a leak.

rules.message: SSO is on the roadmap, not in the product. A security reviewer will treat this sentence as a commitment.
rules.fix: "SSO is on the roadmap." No date.

rules.message: Contract language. Only the SLA makes commitments.
rules.fix: "designed for" or "targets", and link the SLA.

rules.message: Ambiguous. Engineering means under five seconds; buyers hear instant. Warn, not blocker: some uses are fine, so read the sentence.
